# 72-Hour Power-Outage Home Prep

Keep a household safe and comfortable through an outage up to 72 hours. Temperate climate, no backup generator. Work sections in order; earlier ones matter most.

## Water
Store 4 litres of water per person daily — 12 litres per person over 72 hours. Half for drinking, half for cooking and basic hygiene. Use food-grade containers, keep out of direct sunlight, replace every 6 months. Before a forecast storm, also fill the bathtub; its water flushes toilets and washes, never drink it.

## Food
Keep a dedicated shelf of non-perishable food for 3 days: canned beans, canned fish, peanut butter, crackers, dried fruit, shelf-stable milk. Pick no-cook foods; own a manual can opener — electric ones fail. Eat perishable fridge food first, then freezer food, then the emergency shelf.

## Fridge/freezer
Unopened, a fridge stays safe about 4 hours. A full freezer holds temperature about 48 hours, half-full about 24 — so keep it full and consolidated, padding space with frozen-water containers. Keep both doors closed; tape a reminder note on each. Discard perishable food over 2 hours above 4°C; when in doubt, throw it out.

## Light
Use battery LED lanterns or headlamps as primary light; avoid candles, a leading cause of outage house fires. Keep at least one light per person plus two spare battery sets each. Put one headlamp by each bed, one lantern in the kitchen, findable in the dark.

## Heat/safety
Never run a camping stove, barbecue, or generator indoors, in a garage, or near a window — all make carbon monoxide, odourless and potentially fatal. Install at least one battery carbon-monoxide alarm on each floor where people sleep. In cold, pick one small south-facing room, close its door, gather everyone; layered clothing and blankets beat any improvised heater. If indoor temperature drops below 10°C and you can't stay warm, move to a warming centre or neighbour's home.

## Communication
Keep a battery or hand-crank radio for emergency broadcasts; learn your local emergency station's frequency beforehand. Charge every phone and power bank when a storm is forecast; a full 20,000 mAh bank recharges a typical phone about 4 times. Set your phone to low-power mode at the start. Agree beforehand on one out-of-area contact everyone texts — texts beat voice calls on congested networks.

## Medical
Keep a first-aid kit and a 7-day supply of every prescription, rotated to stay in date. Refrigerated medication like insulin usually stays usable at room temperature up to 28 days, but confirm your medication's rule with a pharmacist first. Write pharmacy, doctor, and poison-control numbers on paper; a dead phone is no phone book.

## Recovery
Wait 5 minutes before switching major appliances on, letting the grid stabilise. Check the freezer: food still holding ice crystals refreezes safely. Restock used supplies within one week, water and batteries first. Note on one page what was missing or awkward, and fix at least one gap before the next outage.
hardConstraintNote: Remains a self-contained instruction document: keeps the title plus all eight section headers (Water, Food, Fridge/freezer, Light, Heat/safety, Communication, Medical, Recovery), and every instruction is a complete, followable imperative needing no external reference. No fact was reduced to a fragment that loses actionable meaning; quantities keep units, thresholds keep comparators. Kept in prose rather than article-less headline telegraphy to stay within the low-hard-constraint-risk line-editor lens instead of crossing into the restructurer's elevated risk to the self-contained constraint.
rationale: Pure sentence-level tightening of artifact/GUIDE.md (the artifact my prompt authorized me to read), no document restructure. Moves: (1) deleted throat-clearing framing and rewrote each section as direct imperatives; (2) passive/hedged clauses to active; (3) cut redundant connectives/qualifiers ('as much as possible', 'because each of these produces', 'even if some of the space is taken up by', 'sufficient for', 'roughly'); (4) merged adjacent clauses with semicolons/em-dashes; (5) unit symbols (degrees Celsius to C, milliamp-hours to mAh) and contractions. Every quantity, duration, temperature, listed item and ordered step survives and is recoverable — I re-walked the full fact set (72h; 4 L/person/day and 12 L total; 6-month rotation; bathtub for flushing+washing not drinking; 6-item food list; no-cook + manual opener; fridge-then-freezer-then-shelf; 4h/48h/24h/2h/4C; LED-not-candles; 1 light/person + 2 spare battery sets; headlamp-per-bed + kitchen lantern; CO sources/odourless/fatal; CO alarm per sleeping floor; south-facing room + layers; 10C threshold; radio + local frequency; 20000 mAh ~4x; low-power mode; out-of-area text contact; first-aid + 7-day meds + rotate; insulin 28 days + pharmacist; paper phone numbers; 5-min wait; ice-crystal refreeze; one-week restock water+batteries first; one-page after-action note). A faithful line-edit of the 730 baseline cannot reach sub-472 because the sub-526 gains came from restructurer-lens moves (telegraphic bullets, section merges) outside this lens; and this seat reads GUIDE.md, not the folded best, so the compose-on-472 path that prices the line-editor's ~445-455 ceiling 'from the 472 best' is unavailable here. I do not claim OT-4 met; I flag OT-4 for the compose/restructure family and offer this as the honest independent line-editor floor from baseline.
